explanation: The left hand is traditionally reserved for personal hygiene and the right hand for eating, greeting, and handling food — a distinction rooted in Islamic practice that is widely observed in the UAE, including by many non-Muslim residents in mixed settings. Eating or passing food with the left hand in front of others is considered impolite, though practical exceptions are made for people who cannot use their right hand.
local_tip: Eat, pass dishes, and accept food with your right hand, even if you're left-handed.

also_check.note: The left hand is reserved for toilet hygiene, so eating or passing food with it is considered unclean.
There is no stigma around which hand you use; chopstick technique matters far more than left- or right-handedness.
Left-handed eating carries no cultural stigma at all.

sources.title: Why Left-Handed Eating Is Frowned Upon In The Middle East
